fact_en:
Why does a carabao lick soil?

A carabao sometimes licks salty soil or rocks to get minerals that the grass it eats doesn't fully provide.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga tilapan sa kalabaw ang yuta?

Usahay tilapan sa kalabaw ang parat nga yuta o bato aron makakuha og mineral nga kulang sa kumpay nga iyang gikaon.

findings.note: title_bis "Kabaw Dili Asin Yuta" for title_en "Carabao Licks Salty Soil" — the verb is gone and `Dili` (= not) sits in its place, so the title reads as a negation of the very fact the card teaches (looks like a corrupted `Dila`). Body is correct (`tilapan ... ang parat nga yuta`), but the title alone states the opposite.

fact_en:
Why do some birds have such bright feathers?

To attract a mate! Many colorful birds show off their bright feathers to win a partner.
fact_bis:
Nganong mabulukon ang balhibo sa langgam?

Aron makadani og kapikas! Gipasundayag sa daghang langgam ang ilang masilaw nga balhibo.

findings.note: title_bis "Makulay nga Buhok sa Pag-ikid" for title_en "Bright Feathers Attract Mates" — `buhok` is HAIR; birds' feathers are `balhibo`, which is what the body (and the terms list) correctly uses. Lower severity than the others since the body restores it, but it is a title naming a different thing, same class as the iro case.

fact_en:
Can moths hear bats coming?

Yes! Some moths can actually hear a bat's calls. When they sense one coming, they swerve, dive, or fly away to escape — bats and moths keep getting better at this game!
fact_bis:
Makadungog ba ang anunugba sa kabog?

Oo! Adunay mga anunugba nga makadungog sa tingog sa kabog. Kung mabati nila nga nagpaduol kini, kalit silang moliko, mohulog, o molupad palayo — parehong nag-ayo ang kabog ug anunugba niini nga dula!

findings.note: title_bis "Kagaw Makadungog Paniki" for "Moths Hear Bats" — kagaw is germ/microbe, not moth. Corroborated: elsewhere in this very batch (ffct-03225) and across the corpus kagaw is consistently used for germs, while every other moth card titles it anunugba or gamugamo. Title reads "Germs Can Hear Bats"; only the body (anunugba) names the right animal.

fact_en:
What is a rooster?

A rooster is a male chicken with a colorful comb on its head. It's famous for its loud crow, especially in the morning!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang sunoy?

Ang sunoy usa ka laking manok nga may bulokon nga palong sa ulo. Bantogan siya sa iyang kusog nga tuktugaok, ilabi na sa buntag!

findings.note: title_bis "Tandok" for "Rooster" — tandok is the traditional cupping/suction horn, not a rooster. Body correctly says sunoy. Corpus check: "Tandok" occurs exactly once (this card); all other rooster cards title it Tandang or use sunoy, so this looks like a one-off corruption of tandang.

fact_en:
What is a locust?

A locust is a kind of grasshopper that gathers together into huge, moving swarms!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang balang?

Ang balang usa ka matang sa apan nga nagatapok sa dakong panon o langkay!

findings.note: title_bis "Panon sa mga Dulaw" for "Locust Swarms" — dulaw is turmeric/yellow (corpus elsewhere: "modulaw" = turn yellow), not locust (dulon/balang). Body correctly says balang/apan. "Dulaw" as a locust appears only here; other locust cards use Balang or Locust.

title_bis: Mugbo nga Kinabuhi sa Worker Ant
fact_en: Worker ants live much shorter lives than the queen — many survive just a few months, while the queen can live for years since all new ants come from her.
fact_bis: Mas mubo ang kinabuhi sa worker ant kaysa sa reyna — daghang worker ang mabuhi lang ug pipila ka bulan, samtang ang reyna mabuhi og pipila ka tuig kay gikan kaniya ang tanang bag-ong langgam.

findings.note: EN: "...the queen can live for years since all new ants come from her." BIS: "...kay gikan kaniya ang tanang bag-ong langgam." In Cebuano `langgam` = BIRD (Tagalog false friend, where langgam = ant); the corpus uses langgam ~1000x correctly for birds. The fact-bearing clause therefore says the ant queen produces all the new BIRDS, and the card never names ants in Cebuano (it keeps English "worker ant" and "reyna", nothing restores subay/hulmigas). Same false-friend defect appears in ffct-00110, titled "Langgam sa Matag Tawo" for an ants card.

fact_en: Sweating cools you down after playing outside, but you must drink water to replace what you lost and avoid dangerous dehydration.
fact_bis: Ang paghuyop nagpalamig kanimo human maglaro, apan kinahanglan ka moinom og tubig aron mapulihan ang nawala ug malikayan ang delikado nga dehydration.

findings.note: EN: "Sweating cools you down after playing outside, but you must drink water to replace what you lost..." BIS: "Ang paghuyop nagpalamig kanimo human maglaro...". `paghuyop` is BLOWING (air out of the mouth) — the corpus uses it correctly that way elsewhere (ffct-05051 paghuyop sa samad, ffct-05080 elephant blowing air). Sweat (singot / pagsingot) never appears anywhere in the card, and title_bis is only "Pagkawala sa Tubig". A child reading only the Cebuano learns that BLOWING cools you and never learns that sweating is what cools you and what drains the water that must be replaced — the card's whole causal fact is gone. Same family as the known `pagpanghupaw` (sighing) defect.

fact_en: When a wasp stings, it releases a special smell that calls other wasps to attack too — that's why disturbing a nest can be dangerous!
fact_bis: Kung manukol ang putyukan, mobuga kini og espesyal nga baho nga magtawag sa ubang putyukan aron mosulong sab — mao nga delikado ang paghasi sa salag!

findings.note: English card is about a WASP ("When a wasp stings, it releases a special smell that calls other wasps..."). The Cebuano calls it "putyukan" throughout — title_bis "Alarma sa Putyukan" and body "Kung manukol ang putyukan... magtawag sa ubang putyukan" — and putyukan/putyokan is the honeybee, not a wasp. Nothing in the card corrects it, so a child reading only the Cebuano learns this about bees. This corpus already has distinct Cebuano words for wasp (kagitgit, tambuboan, tambubuk) plus untranslated "wasp", so putyukan here is a wrong-animal swap, not regional usage.

fact_en: A Chihuahua and a Saint Bernard are both the same species -- dogs! Yet they can differ hugely in size, from tiny to giant.
fact_bis: Ang Chihuahua ug Saint Bernard parehong aso -- usa ra ka species! Apan lahi kaayo sila sa gidak-on, gikan gamay hangtod dako kaayo.

findings.note: EN "A Chihuahua and a Saint Bernard are both the same species -- dogs!" becomes "Ang Chihuahua ug Saint Bernard parehong aso" — in Cebuano aso is SMOKE, not dog. Corpus check is decisive: 213 cards use aso and every other one means smoke (cigarette smoke, cooking smoke, onion fumes), while dog is iro in 188 cards. The sentence carrying the fact tells a Cebuano-only child the two breeds are "both smoke"; only the title (Gidak-on sa Iro) hints at dogs.

fact_en:
How long can a land tortoise live?

Some land tortoises have lived almost 180 years, making them among the oldest animals ever recorded!
fact_bis:
Hangtod kanus-a mabuhi ang baw-i sa yuta?

Ang ubang mga baw-i sa yuta narekord nga nabuhi og halos 180 ka tuig, usa sa labing tigulang nga mga hayop!

findings.note: Card is about LAND tortoises living ~180 years, but title_bis is "180 Tuig sa Kinabuhi sa Pawikan" — pawikan is the sea turtle, which does not live 180 years. Corpus check: of 25 tortoise cards, 23 use bao/pagong/tortoise and only this one and ffct-02706 use pawikan, while pawikan is the sea-turtle word in 158 cards (incl. ffct-03666 prosthetic flipper). The body's "baw-i sa yuta" is correct, so the defect is the title attributing the number to the wrong animal.

fact_en:
What's the difference between shivering and goosebumps?

Shivering and goosebumps are different reflexes to cold! Shivering is muscle movement that makes heat; goosebumps make hair stand up to trap heat near the skin.
fact_bis:
Unsay kalainan sa kurog ug kilabot?

Lahi nga reflex ang kurog ug kilabot bisan pareho silang tungod sa bugnaw! Ang kurog kay paglihok sa kaunoran nga naghimo og kainit; ang kilabot kay pagtindog sa balhibo aron makakuha og kainit duol sa panit.

findings.note: title_bis "Pagkurog ug Gansa" renders "goosebumps" as gansa = a GOOSE, a different animal, for a card about shivering vs goosebumps. Corpus check: 9 cards use gansa and the other 8 are all real geese cards (honking, V-formation, ducks-and-geese), so gansa means goose everywhere else in this corpus. The body uses the correct word kilabot, but the header a child reads first says "shivering and goose".

fact_en: If a cut is deep or won't stop bleeding, tell an adult and ask for help right away!
fact_bis: Kon lawom ang samad o dili mohunong ang dugo, dayon pangayo og tabang sa tigulang!

findings.note: title_bis "Lalom Samat Kaban" for "Deep Cut Tell Adult": kaban is a chest/box/vault (used correctly that way in ffct-00441 "sama sa kaban nga nanalipod"), never "adult", and samat is not a word (samad = cut). Same title bug recurs corpus-wide: "206 Bones in Adults" -> "206 Bukog Kaban" in both ffct-05855 and ffct-09441. Here the card never says hamtong anywhere — the body says tigulang (an old person) — so "adult" is not restored, and the title reads as a deep chest wound.
